report.summary: Two separate causes. The app's book listing ignores the owner (list_books in app/main.py:147-150 runs an unfiltered SELECT), so one user sees another user's books; that breaks the API isolation test and the new-user empty-state UI test, and it is the first thing to fix. The two UI add-book tests fail because the page object clicks get_by_test_id("add-books") while the template uses data-testid="add-book", a test-side locator typo that is quick to fix.

causes.title: GET /api/books and the /books page list every user's books
causes.explanation: list_books(user_id) accepts the user id but never uses it: the query is 'SELECT * FROM books ORDER BY id' with no owner_id filter. Every logged-in user therefore receives all books in the database. get_own_book does filter by owner_id, so single-book GET/PUT/DELETE correctly return 404 for other users, which is why only the listing leaks. The API test sees the other user's book id in the list. The UI test's new user is shown a book created by a different test user, so the empty state never renders. This is a deterministic bug, not a timing issue: the failure appears whenever another user's book exists in the same database.
evidence: tests\api\test_books_api.py:42: AssertionError  assert book["id"] not in other_ids  ->  assert 2 not in [1, 2]
app/main.py:147-150: def list_books(user_id: int) -> list[dict]: rows = conn.execute("SELECT * FROM books ORDER BY id").fetchall()
app/main.py:163-166: get_own_book filters with "WHERE id = ? AND owner_id = ?", so the owner check exists for single books but not for the list
Login UI aria snapshot for a freshly registered user: row "From API-d58f5c6c Robot Delete" appears under the table, and the empty-state element is not found
app/main.py:253: render_books passes list_books(user["id"]) to the template, so the leak reaches the UI
causes.suggested_fix: Change the query in list_books to 'SELECT * FROM books WHERE owner_id = ? ORDER BY id' and pass user_id as the parameter. Then add an API test that a second user's list is empty, and check that the empty state renders for a new user.

causes.title: Page object clicks data-testid "add-books" but the button is "add-book"
causes.explanation: BooksPage.add in tests/support/pages.py clicks get_by_test_id("add-books"). The Add book button in books.html has data-testid="add-book". The locator matches nothing, so Playwright waits 5 s and then times out before any app behavior is exercised. The app is correct here; the test support code has a typo. Both UI add-book tests fail at the same line, and the same locator is used by the page object, so fixing it in one place should unblock both.
evidence: tests\ui\test_books_ui.py:13 / tests\support\pages.py:44: self.page.get_by_test_id("add-books").click()  ->  waiting for get_by_test_id("add-books")  ->  Locator.click: Timeout 5000ms exceeded.
tests\ui\test_books_ui.py:42 (test_future_year_shows_error_and_keeps_input) fails at the same locator, before its assertions run
causes.suggested_fix: In tests/support/pages.py line 44, change get_by_test_id("add-books") to get_by_test_id("add-book"). Re-run the two UI tests. The future-year test's remaining assertions (error text, kept title value, no row) look consistent with app/main.py:328-332 and the template, so they should be checked once the click works.
